justifications.functional_suitability: Billing & Admin Suite (Admission Management Service, Billing Management Service), Clinical Workspace, and Patient Portal's Appointment Self-Service Module cover most requirements. Gaps: no resource clash check component, no insurance claim submission component, and the Insurance Payment Gateways are only inbound; no explicit EMR audit-trail UI.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Patient Cache Manager (Redis), Core Datastore Read Replicas with CQRS, and asynchronous WORM logging via Secure Message Broker support the <1s target. Gaps: the cache is only in the Patient Portal, not Clinical Workspace; no autoscaling or load figures; HSM calls on the critical path.
justifications.compatibility: FHIR Integration Engine (FHIR Router, FHIR Resource Mapper) and API Gateway expose HL7 FHIR for External Labs/Imaging; IdP uses OIDC. Gaps: FHIR flow is inbound only, no outbound lab/imaging requests, insurance claim format standards (X12) unspecified, and the mapper has limited detail.
justifications.usability: Patient Portal (Patient Web Frontend, mobile-responsive), Clinical Workspace (EMR Presentation Component), and Billing & Admin Suite serve the three user groups, and Audit Query & Export serves auditors. Gaps: no UI component for admin/billing, no accessibility or multilingual provisions, and sparse interface detail.
justifications.reliability: Secure Message Broker prevents log loss and Core Datastore has Read Replicas. But no active-active deployment, failover, multi-region replication, backup or DR is shown. Single Primary Write Datastore, single HSM and API Gateway are SPOFs, so 99.99% is not demonstrably achievable.
justifications.security: Strong mechanisms: IdP with MFA, Security Filter JWT/scope checks, mTLS with SPIFFE/SPIRE, TLS 1.3, HSM with FIPS 140-2 Level 3 and key rotation, and WORM Audit Logging Service with signing and S3 Object Lock. Covers authentication, authorization, encryption, integrity and accountability.
justifications.maintainability: Clear container decomposition (Patient Portal, Clinical Workspace, Billing & Admin Suite, FHIR Integration Engine, Core Datastore) with a gateway and well-separated audit pipeline components. Minor gaps: shared Core Datastore couples services, and some component technologies are vague (Kubernetes as a component technology).
justifications.portability: Kubernetes containers and MinIO / S3 Object Lock WORM storage suggest hybrid on-prem and AWS operation. Gaps: API Gateway labeled Kubernetes / AWS, a hardware HSM is tied to location, no deployment view for on-prem-k8s versus eu-central-1, and no infrastructure abstraction is described.

tradeoffs: CQRS read replicas improve speed but risk stale data
PERF-01.justification: CQRS read replicas and a low-latency gateway help, but the clinical path has no cache, no scaling or load mechanism, and replica staleness is unaddressed. P95 under 1 s for 500 concurrent users is plausible but unproven.

sensitivity_points: No queue or buffering for FHIR bursts
tradeoffs: Direct persistence is simple but couples ingestion load to EMR performance
PERF-02.justification: FHIR results go through the gateway and straight to the single primary datastore with no buffering, back-pressure, or isolation. Burst ingestion could degrade EMR reads. Read replicas offer partial protection only.

sensitivity_points: No failover or traffic-steering mechanism shown
tradeoffs: Hybrid footprint offers resilience but multi-site consistency is undefined
AVAIL-01.justification: Hybrid regions are targeted, but the model shows no active-active deployment, global traffic routing, or synchronous replication. A 1-minute failover with zero data loss is not demonstrated. The single primary is a risk.

sensitivity_points: No database HA or automatic failover shown
No idempotency or retry mechanism for claims
tradeoffs: Simple synchronous write path lacks safe-retry guarantees
AVAIL-02.justification: A single PostgreSQL master has no described standby promotion, and no idempotency keys, outbox, or retry logic for claims. Lost or duplicated claims are not prevented. The claim recovery target is not supported.

sensitivity_points: Billing service handles gateway integration directly
tradeoffs: Fewer components reduce complexity but weaken isolation of integrations
MOD-01.justification: There is no insurance integration or adapter component. Claim submission is implicit within the Billing Management Service, so adding a clearinghouse would change billing logic. The EMR is likely unaffected because it is a separate container, but confinement to one integration component is not achieved.

sensitivity_points: Shared Core Datastore schema across containers
Demographics ownership spread across several components
tradeoffs: Shared datastore eases consistency but couples changes across containers
MOD-02.justification: Changes touch the datastore schema, admission service, UI, and audit emission. That is feasible within three components if scoped well, but demographic ownership is unclear and the shared schema creates ripple risk.

sensitivity_points: Gateway must verify the MFA claim
No alerting component for failed logins
tradeoffs: External IdP offloads MFA but adds a dependency on its availability
SEC-01.justification: The IdP with MFA and gateway Security Filter validating JWT and MFA deny access without the second factor. However, there is no security alerting or monitoring component, and auth failures are not explicitly routed to the audit service, so the 1-minute alert is unmet.

sensitivity_points: Asynchronous logging may miss reads on failure
tradeoffs: Async audit lowers latency but risks audit gaps
SEC-02.justification: A strong tamper-evident trail exists: Kafka buffering, HSM signing, and S3 Object Lock. Scope-based checks exist, but no treatment-relationship policy enforcement is shown, and the 10-year retention and 100% read-audit guarantee are not explicit.
